subject: COBOL words
notes: Rule: `OK §8.3.2.2 1)` "If the CALL statement, CANCEL statement, or program-address-identifier specifies a program-prototype-name, the naming convention and mapping used for the program-name is determined by the entry convention indicated by the description of the program to be called, as specified in 12.3.8, REPOSITORY paragraph, General rule 10;". The only entry convention is COBOL (ENTRY-CONVENTION IS <other> refused COBOL2385, DOC-A.1-64), so the rule reduces to: the prototype's externalized name (literal-3 when written, else the word — §12.3.8.4 GR10 NOTE 1) is what CALL / CANCEL / ADDRESS OF PROGRAM reach. conformance:cases/8.3.2.2-User-defined-words/pb237_program_prototype (expected values derived in its header from §12.3.8.4 GR10 and §14.9.4.4 GR3 b)) exercises CALL PB237ADD, CALL "PB237ADD" AS PB237ADD, CALL SCALE-IT where `PROGRAM SCALE-IT AS "PB237MUL"` activates PB237MUL, and CANCEL PB237ADD SCALE-IT; conformance:cases/8.4.3.13-Program-address-identifier/pb549_program_address_identifier arm 4 pins ADDRESS OF PROGRAM PB549P reaching externalized name "PB549X" (§8.4.3.13.4 GR2). Both goldens state their expected output as derived from the rules, never measured.
